text.p: Morgan Stanley said it has raised its earnings estimates for Brazilian pulp and paper maker Aracruz Celulose to $0.72 per American Depositary Receipt (ADR) from $0.45 for 1997 and to $1.78 from $1.65 for 1998.

-- "The main reasons for the increases are higher pulp price projections and stronger-than-expected first quarter 1997 operating results," Morgan Stanley analysts Hillary Kircher Peruzzi and Clicia Morales said in a report.

-- Despite the improvements in the pulp market, the analysts maintained their neutral rating on Aracruz's ADR due to the valuation of the stock, now trading at close to its 52-week high on expectations of increasing pulp prices.
-- They also said they are raising their estimates for Aracruz's realized price per export ton to $468 from $431 in 1997 and to $583 from $575 in 1998.
-- "We now believe that there is a higher probability that the recent pulp price increases will hold throughout the summer," they wrote.
-- Pulp inventories have been coming down in recent months due to strong demand and paper shipments to the U.S. and Europe have been exceptionally strong year-to-date, they added.
-- The analysts said the key concern among investors, especially in Europe, is to what extent the rebound in shipments reflects an rebuilding of inventories by customers.
-- Aracruz' Level Three ADR was up 1/8 at 20-1/2 in New York, while its preferred B share was up 0.46 percent at 2.18 reais in Sao Paulo at 1338 local time/1238 EDT.
